chunks: From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Habib Al-Sijistani, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

It is written in the Torah, in what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, whispered to Musa (peace be upon him): 'O Musa! Withhold your anger from the one whom I have given you authority over, I shall restrain My anger from you.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Torah say about controlling anger to gain God's mercy?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the concept of *al-Ghadab* (anger) as a critical spiritual trait, linking the Prophetic example of Musa (AS) to the broader Shia emphasis on self-restraint (*hilm*) as a prerequisite for divine proximity. It underscores the reciprocal nature of divine mercy, where human emotional discipline invites God's restraint from punishment, a theme central to Shia ethical theology (*akhlaq*).
